title: bioAffinity Technologies Publishes New Clinical Framework Addressing Growing Market for Pulmonary Nodule Risk Stratification and Early Lung Cancer Detection Using CyPath® Lung
summary: Comprehensive clinical review outlines specialty-specific approaches for integrating the test’s lung microenvironment analysis into…...
body_text: bioAffinity Technologies Publishes New Clinical Framework Addressing Growing Market for Pulmonary Nodule Risk Stratification and Early Lung Cancer Detection Using CyPath® Lung July 27, 2026 8:08am EDT Comprehensive clinical review outlines specialty-specific approaches for integrating the test’s lung microenvironment analysis into diagnostic pathway Framework includes protocols for pulmonology, primary care and oncology practices for detection of lung cancer and surveillance of survivors SAN ANTONIO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- bioAffinity Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: BIAF; BIAFW) , a biotechnology company focused on noninvasive diagnostics and early cancer detection, today announced the publication of a comprehensive clinical review and white paper authored by Chief Medical Officer Gordon H. Downie, MD, PhD, that presents a practical clinical framework for incorporating CyPath® Lung into pulmonary nodule evaluation and cancer surveillance. Titled " Lung Nodules, Lung Microenvironment, Predictive Models and Clinician Risk Stratification Using CyPath® Lung Testing for Early Diagnosis of Lung Cancer ," the paper examines the growing clinical challenge of evaluating pulmonary nodules as lung cancer screening expands, incidental findings increase, artificial intelligence identifies even more incidental nodules, and more patients require long-term surveillance following cancer treatment. "Pulmonary medicine is entering a new era in which clinicians are evaluating more pulmonary nodules than ever before, driving a rapidly growing need for better risk stratification," said Maria Zannes, President and Chief Executive Officer of bioAffinity Technologies. "Dr. Downie's white paper demonstrates how CyPath® Lung can provide physicians with clinically meaningful information that complements imaging and clinical assessment, helping them make more confident decisions about which patients require invasive procedures and which can be safely monitored." Drawing on the three years of commercial experience since CyPath® Lung entered the market, the publication discusses how the noninvasive test has demonstrated consistent clinical performance in helping physicians stratify malignancy risk and guide patient management, including clinical case studies illustrating how CyPath® Lung helped clarify challenging cases in which imaging findings and predictive models alone produced uncertain or conflicting assessments. The publication explores how advances in understanding the lung microenvironment are reshaping the evaluation of pulmonary nodules. Unlike blood-based diagnostics, CyPath® Lung analyzes sputum collected directly from the lungs, providing objective, real-time information from the lung microenvironment to help clarify complex or conflicting clinical presentations. The paper also reviews the strengths and limitations of existing predictive models and emphasizes that no single diagnostic tool should be used in isolation. Instead, it proposes specialty-specific clinical pathways that integrate CyPath® Lung into three care settings: Primary care practices managing incidentally discovered pulmonary nodules Pulmonary nodule programs and interventional pulmonology practices evaluating patients for biopsy Oncology practices conducting surveillance of cancer survivors "Every patient presents a unique clinical picture," Dr. Downie said. "The objective is not to replace clinician gestalt or existing guidelines, but to provide an additional data point when clinical findings are uncertain or contradictory. CyPath® Lung’s interrogation of the lung microenvironment gives physicians information that has not previously been available through traditional imaging or blood-based testing." The white paper highlights the growing recognition that the lung possesses a unique microenvironment distinct from blood, reflecting local immune responses, inflammation, genetic alterations and tumor biology. By evaluating sputum directly from the lungs, CyPath® Lung measures these biologic changes and identifies porphyrin-labeled malignant cells through proprietary flow cytometry and artificial intelligence analysis. The complete white paper is available at https://bit.ly/cypath-lung-whitepaper3 . About CyPath® Lung CyPath® Lung by bioAffinity Technologies is a noninvasive test designed to improve the early detection of lung cancer in patients at high risk for the disease. CyPath® Lung uses advanced flow cytometry and proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) to identify cell populations in patient sputum that indicate malignancy. CyPath® Lung incorporates a fluorescent porphyrin that is preferentially taken up by cancer and cancer-related cells. In a published clinical trial of high-risk patients, CyPath® Lung demonstrated 92% sensitivity, 87% specificity, 88% accuracy and 99% negative predictive value (NPV) in detecting lung cancer in patients at high risk for the disease who had small indeterminate lung nodules less than 20 millimeters. The high NPV gives physicians greater confidence that a negative result is truly negative, potentially sparing patients from unnecessary invasive and costly procedures. CyPath® Lung is marketed as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT) and is not intended for use as a sole diagnostic tool and should be considered alongside other clinical findings. About bioAffinity Technologies, Inc. bioAffinity Technologies, Inc. addresses the need for noninvasive diagnosis of early-stage cancer and other diseases of the lung and broad-spectrum cancer treatments. The Company’s first product, CyPath® Lung, is a noninvasive test that has shown high sensitivity, specificity and accuracy for the detection of early-stage lung cancer. CyPath® Lung is marketed as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT) by Precision Pathology Laboratory Services, a subsidiary of bioAffinity Technologies. LDTs are overseen under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), which are administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. For more information, visit www.bioaffinitytech.com . title: Top 5 Fleet Fuel Card Programs for Businesses
summary: We rank the top 5 fleet fuel card programs on savings, fees, and acceptance. See why AtoB averages 42¢/gallon with zero network limits. Compare now.
body_text: Fuel is one of the largest controllable expenses across fleet operations, yet many fleets still rely on generic payment cards that lack the controls needed to manage fuel spending, driver purchases, and operating costs. A fleet fuel card program is built to solve exactly these challenges by combining payments, reporting, and controls into one system. This guide explains how to evaluate the right fleet fuel card for your business, compares leading providers, and outlines how modern platforms help fleet managers track fuel, improve fuel efficiency, and reduce overall fleet fuel expenses. Why Your Fuel Card Program Can Make or Break Fleet Margins Small per-gallon differences compound quickly across thousands of fill-ups each year, significantly impacting overall fleet management costs . ATRI's annual operational cost survey found that fuel averaged 48.1 cents per mile in 2024 1, roughly 21% of the $2.26 total cost per mile for motor carriers. For fleet owners managing tight operating margins, the right fuel card program can improve cost visibility, reduce fraud exposure, and support stronger trip-level profitability. Meanwhile, standard payment tools lack the visibility needed to manage fuel spend effectively. Here's the difference: Business credit cards typically capture only total transaction values Fleet fuel cards capture detailed data, including gallons, location, and driver usage Beyond discounts, the right fleet card program protects margins by helping to prevent fuel card fraud , enforce spend controls, and streamline accounting. These are benefits that generic payment cards never offer. What to Look for in a Fleet Fuel Card Program for Businesses Several critical factors separate the best fuel cards for business from programs that create more problems than they solve. The right program for your fleet depends on network access, cost structure, controls, and reporting capabilities, especially when evaluating the best fuel cards for truckers operating across different routes and fueling patterns. Network Coverage and Acceptance A key consideration is where cards can be used. Some programs restrict purchases to independent gas stations or branded fuel stations, while others provide broader access. Open-loop cards backed by Mastercard or Visa work at nearly any truck stop nationwide. Closed-loop cards restrict purchases to a specific brand. Fuel cards are accepted at a wide range of locations, including major truck stops and independent fuel stations, helping fleets avoid detours and maintain efficiency. Spend Controls and Fraud Prevention Fuel cards offer built-in controls that standard payment tools do not. Look for features such as: Dollar limits - Set maximum transaction amounts per purchase Gallon caps - Prevent excessive fuel purchases beyond tank capacity Time-of-day restrictions - Block purchases during off-hours Merchant category filtering - Limit purchases to fuel-only transactions Meanwhile, advanced programs add telematics integration to verify vehicle location at the point of sale and confirm purchases do not exceed tank capacity. Preventing misuse ensures that fuel savings are not offset by unnecessary expenses. Reporting, Fees, and Credit Requirements The best fuel card for your business should provide clear reporting and transparent pricing. Make sure to evaluate: Monthly account fees, a small fee per card, and setup costs to avoid the hidden costs of fuel cards Transaction or processing charges Reporting tools for tracking fuel receipts and usage Confirm whether a personal guarantee or credit check is required, as many fleets prefer net 30 fuel cards to limit liability. Understanding the type of card you choose is important, as it determines both flexibility and cost. Top 5 Business Fuel Card Programs These five commercial fuel card providers were evaluated on discount depth, network coverage, fee structure, and fraud protection to determine the best fleet management fuel cards . AtoB AtoB provides a modern fuel card for your business designed to simplify fuel management. Cards can be used anywhere Mastercard is accepted, including gas stations and truck stops Telematics-based controls include location validation, fuel-level tracking, and Card Unlock Built-in reporting to support fleet management and expense tracking Supports both prepaid and credit-based options For professional drivers, AtoB offers two cards: Flex provides credit with Experian, while Unlimited offers prepaid spending with fast approval. The AtoB Discount Network delivers average truck diesel savings of 42¢ per gallon (up to $2.00)* at participating truck stops. WEX Fleet Card WEX provides access to the WEX Nationwide Savings Network and offers reporting, controls, and fuel management tools for commercial fleets. Savings structures vary based on fuel volume and network usage, which may make costs less predictable for smaller or growing fleets. Businesses evaluating the WEX Fleet Card should review current pricing and rebate information directly through WEX. Fuelman Fuelman offers fuel management tools and rebate programs through its network of participating fuel locations. Costs and savings may vary depending on network usage, billing structure, and monthly fuel volume. Shell Fleet Navigator Shell Fleet Navigator primarily focuses on branded network fuel discounts and maintenance-related savings at participating locations. Larger rebate opportunities are generally tied to higher monthly fuel volume and consistent network usage. Coast Fleet Card Coast provides Visa-backed fleet payment tools with fuel rewards and expense tracking features for service-based fleets. The platform may be a stronger fit for local and regional operations than for fleets running long-haul routes. How AtoB Guides Drivers to Savings AtoB functions as a unified fleet management platform extending beyond basic gas only credit cards by combining fuel payments, controls, reporting, and fleet expense management . The process works in five steps: Apply for an AtoB fuel card online. Select your card type based on whether you need credit reporting or prepaid flexibility. Configure controls, including spend limits, merchant restrictions, and telematics-based fraud prevention. Drivers locate savings using the AtoB Driver App to find fleet fuel discounts along their routes. Monitor performance through real-time visibility, automated International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) reporting , and AI-powered spend insights. AtoB's spend management platform integrates Fleet, Business Expense, and Payroll cards into a single system to simplify fuel expense oversight. Frequently Asked Questions What is a fleet fuel card program? A fleet fuel card program is a payment system built for businesses operating vehicles, providing spend controls, fuel discounts, fraud prevention, and detailed transaction reporting that standard credit cards do not offer. How much can a business save with a fleet fuel card program? Savings depend on fleet size and fuel volume. AtoB customers receive average truck diesel savings of 42¢ per gallon (up to $2.00)* at participating truck stops. Can I use a fleet fuel card at any truck stop? Acceptance depends on card type. Open-loop cards backed by Mastercard work at nearly any truck stop nationwide. Closed-loop cards are limited to their respective networks. Do fleet fuel card programs require a credit check? Not all programs require credit checks. Prepaid options like AtoB Unlimited do not require a credit check, making them ideal for small businesses. What spending controls do fleet fuel card programs offer? Common controls include dollar limits, gallon caps, time restrictions, and fuel type filtering. Advanced programs add telematics-based location and fuel-level validation. Sources TRID TRB. An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking: 2025 Update. https://trid.trb.org/View/2570650 ‍ * Average discount of 42¢ refers to realized average savings per gallon of truck diesel across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner truck stops during H2 2025. The up to discount of $2.00 refers to max realized savings per gallon of truck diesel across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner truck stops during H2 2025. Average discount of 5¢ off per gallon of unleaded is an average across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner gas stations during H2 2025.

title: Public when it should be. Private when it must be. Leena AI launches Group Chat Agent for Slack.
summary: Leena AI's Group Chat Agent for Slack is live. @-mention your AI Colleague in any channel — it answers public questions in place and routes private data to a DM.
body_text: The Group Chat Agent for Slack is live. Your AI Colleague can now be @-mentioned in any channel, private channel, or group DM. We built the AI Colleague to be fast, accurate, and grounded in your own systems. Adoption still plateaued at every deployment. Not because the AI wasn’t good. Because using it meant leaving the conversation you were already in. Copy the thread. Open a DM. Paste. Explain. Wait. Come back. Most employees, most days, just skipped it. Today that’s over. The AI Colleague can now be tagged directly inside Slack channels, private channels, and group DMs. It reads the conversation around your mention — up to 30 messages, or the full thread if that’s where you asked — and answers in place. But the interesting part isn’t that it shows up. It’s that it knows how to behave. Public when it should be General questions get answered in the channel, with sources. Someone asks about the T&E policy — the answer lands where everyone can see it, learn from it, and stop re-asking it next week. Private when it must be Personal questions get quietly redirected to the asker’s DM. Their remaining Q4 budget. Their PTO balance. Their compensation band. All of it lands in their inbox, not the channel. In the channel, only a short handoff note: “Sarah, that’s specific to you — I’ve shared it in your DM.” Private data doesn’t land in a public channel. Not by accident. Not by user error. Not ever. Aware of the conversation, not eavesdropping on it The AI Colleague only responds when you tag it. Regular channel chatter, unrelated threads, file drops that weren’t addressed to it — all ignored. When you do tag it, it reads the recent context. So “summarize the issue above” works. “What did they mean by that deadline?” works. You don’t re-explain what everyone in the channel already knows. One question, both channels The person who asked always gets the full answer in their DM too, with a “view thread” link back to the original mention. If they want to keep going, they can — privately, with the context preserved. You never have to pick between the visibility of a channel and the depth of a DM. You get both. Access control preserved Every knowledge base answer respects the asker’s own permissions. Same rules as in 1:1. Same enterprise-safe promise. New surface. Why this is the shift The AI Colleague isn’t a place employees go. It’s a teammate in the channels they already work in. That’s the whole idea, and it’s the part we couldn’t ship until the routing was right. Presence without judgment is a liability. An AI that answers everything in public, or leaks private data into a channel, doesn’t get to stay in the room. Ours stays because it knows what belongs where. Get started Available today for all customers with GPT and streaming enabled on their AI Colleague. If you’re already running the AI Colleague on Slack, an admin can turn it on by updating the Slack app scopes and inviting it to a channel: /invite @ Full setup guide → docs.leena.ai/docs/group-chat-agent-for-slack
